meanings: to take a lesson or test
calling on someone who is ill
not entirely (used in a negative sentence)
not at all (used with a negative verb)
limited express train (faster than an express train)
to change between buses or trains
counter for decades of ages, eras, etc.
counter for letters, notes, documents, etc.

grammar.title: Experience: たことがある
grammar.explanation:
Use a verb's plain past form plus ことがある to describe an experience at least once. This differs from reporting one particular past event.

Formation: Plain past verb + ことがある / ことがあります. Negative experience: たことがない.

Usage and cautions: This counts an experience at some point before now, not a regularly scheduled habit. It often combines with 一度 or まだ. A specific yesterday event normally uses a simple past sentence. Keep the verb before こと in plain past even when the sentence ending is polite.

examples.ja: 富士山に登ったことがあります。
examples.en: I have climbed Mount Fuji before.

examples.ja: 京都に行ったことがあります。
examples.reading: きょうとにいったことがあります。
examples.en: I have been to Kyoto before.

examples.ja: 飛行機に乗ったことがありません。
examples.reading: ひこうきにのったことがありません。
examples.en: I have never flown on an airplane.

questions.prompt: Choose 'have eaten sushi before'.
choices: 寿司を食べたことがある
寿司を食べることにする
寿司を食べているところだ
寿司を食べなければならない
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “寿司を食べたことがある”. たことがある describes prior experience, not a decision or an action in progress.

questions.prompt: Complete a past experience: この映画を見＿ことがあります。
questions.explanation: Past 見た before ことがあります describes a previous viewing experience; nonpast 見る would not form this pattern.

questions.prompt: Choose “Have you ever made bread?”
choices: パンを作ってもいいですか。
パンを作ったことがありますか。
パンを作るつもりですか。
questions.explanation: 作ったことがありますか asks about experience; the alternatives ask about intention, permission and an invitation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 京都に行ったことがあります。
choices: I have never been to Kyoto.
I have been to Kyoto before.
I plan to go to Kyoto tomorrow.
I go to Kyoto every day.
questions.explanation: “京都に行ったことがあります。” means “I have been to Kyoto before.” in this example. This counts an experience at some point before now, not a regularly scheduled habit.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 飛行機に乗ったことがありません。
choices: I have never flown on an airplane.
I did not board the plane yesterday.
questions.explanation: “飛行機に乗ったことがありません。” means “I have never flown on an airplane.” in this example. This counts an experience at some point before now, not a regularly scheduled habit.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Listing actions: たり
grammar.explanation:
Attach り to the past verb form to give representative examples of activities. End the list with する; it need not describe every activity.

Formation: Plain past + り、plain past + り + する. Inflect the final する to express tense and politeness.

Usage and cautions: The listed activities are examples rather than an exhaustive sequence. A single たり can also suggest “things like”. Do not omit する in the full basic predicate or interpret the order as a strict timetable. Past-looking forms before り do not themselves make the sentence past.

examples.ja: 日曜日は掃除したり料理したりします。
examples.en: On Sundays I do things like cleaning and cooking.

examples.ja: 週末は泳いだり走ったりします。
examples.reading: しゅうまつはおよいだりはしったりします。
examples.en: On weekends I do things like swimming and running.

examples.ja: 昨日は買い物をしたり、友達に会ったりしました。
examples.reading: きのうはかいものをしたり、ともだちにあったりしました。
examples.en: Yesterday I did things like shopping and meeting a friend.

questions.prompt: Complete: 本を読んだり、音楽を聞い＿します。
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “たり”. 聞いた plus り gives 聞いたり, parallel to 読んだり.

questions.prompt: Complete representative activities: 掃除したり、洗濯し＿します。
questions.explanation: 洗濯した + り parallels 掃除したり; final します completes the nonpast list.

questions.prompt: Which ending makes the entire activity list past?
choices: 読んだり書いたりしましょう。
読んだり書いたりしました。
読んだり書いたりします。
読んだり書いたりしません。
questions.explanation: しました supplies past tense for the list; the internal た forms belong to the たり construction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 週末は泳いだり走ったりします。
choices: On weekends I do things like swimming and running.
I always swim before running on weekdays.
I can neither swim nor run.
I swam only once last weekend.
questions.explanation: “週末は泳いだり走ったりします。” means “On weekends I do things like swimming and running.” in this example. The listed activities are examples rather than an exhaustive sequence.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 昨日は買い物をしたり、友達に会ったりしました。
choices: Tomorrow I will only go shopping.
Yesterday I stayed home without seeing anyone.
My friend bought something for me yesterday.
Yesterday I did things like shopping and meeting a friend.
questions.explanation: “昨日は買い物をしたり、友達に会ったりしました。” means “Yesterday I did things like shopping and meeting a friend.” in this example. The listed activities are examples rather than an exhaustive sequence.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Trying an action: てみる
grammar.explanation:
The て-form plus みる means trying something to see what it is like or what happens. It is not necessarily a difficult attempted action.

Formation: Verb て-form + みる. Inflect みる: みた, みたい, みてください.

Usage and cautions: This is doing an action experimentally to learn its result, not merely attempting without success. The auxiliary is usually written in hiragana. Compare ようとする for trying or being about to act. A successful outcome is not guaranteed by てみる.

examples.ja: この靴を履いてみます。
examples.en: I will try on these shoes.

examples.ja: 新しいアプリを使ってみました。
examples.reading: あたらしいアプリをつかってみました。
examples.en: I tried using the new app.

examples.ja: 分からなければ、先生に聞いてみてください。
examples.reading: わからなければ、せんせいにきいてみてください。
examples.en: If you do not understand, try asking the teacher.

questions.prompt: Choose trying a dish to see its taste.
choices: 食べなければならない
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “食べてみる”. てみる presents an action as an experiment or trial.

questions.prompt: Try wearing a hat to see how it looks: 帽子をかぶっ＿。
questions.explanation: かぶってみる is an experimental trial; ておく indicates preparation and てある a resulting prepared state.

questions.prompt: Choose a desire to try making sushi.
choices: 寿司を作ってみたいです。
寿司を作ってあります。
寿司を作らなくてもいいです。
寿司を作ってはいけません。
questions.explanation: てみたい combines experimental てみる with desire たい: wanting to try making it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 新しいアプリを使ってみました。
choices: I was forced to use the new app.
I have never used the new app.
I finished developing the new app.
I tried using the new app.
questions.explanation: “新しいアプリを使ってみました。” means “I tried using the new app.” in this example. This is doing an action experimentally to learn its result, not merely attempting without success.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 分からなければ、先生に聞いてみてください。
choices: The teacher tried to ask me a question.
Please listen to music instead of asking.
If you do not understand, try asking the teacher.
If you understand, do not ask the teacher.
questions.explanation: “分からなければ、先生に聞いてみてください。” means “If you do not understand, try asking the teacher.” in this example. This is doing an action experimentally to learn its result, not merely attempting without success.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Preparation: ておく
grammar.explanation:
Use ておく for an action done in preparation or for leaving a state as it is. In casual speech ておく often contracts to とく.

Formation: Verb て-form + おく. Casual contractions: ておく → とく, でおく → どく.

Usage and cautions: The action is performed for a later need, or an existing state is deliberately left alone. State the future purpose when context might otherwise be unclear. Unlike てある, this construction foregrounds doing or maintaining the action, not merely observing its result.

examples.ja: 旅行の前に切符を買っておきます。
examples.en: I will buy the tickets ahead of the trip.

examples.ja: 会議の前に資料を印刷しておきます。
examples.reading: かいぎのまえにしりょうをいんさつしておきます。
examples.en: I will print the materials before the meeting in preparation.

examples.ja: 窓は開けておいてください。
examples.reading: まどはあけておいてください。
examples.en: Please leave the window open.

questions.prompt: Complete a preparatory action: 資料を読んで＿。
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “おく”. ておく indicates reading ahead for a later purpose.

questions.prompt: Prepare drinks for tomorrow’s guests: 飲み物を買っ＿。
questions.explanation: 買っておく presents buying in advance for the guests; the other choices do not express preparation.

questions.prompt: Choose the casual contraction of 読んでおく.
questions.explanation: でおく contracts to どく, so 読んでおく becomes 読んどく; じゃう contracts でしまう.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 会議の前に資料を印刷しておきます。
choices: I am forbidden to print the materials.
I will print the materials before the meeting in preparation.
I accidentally lost the meeting materials.
questions.explanation: “会議の前に資料を印刷しておきます。” means “I will print the materials before the meeting in preparation.” in this example. The action is performed for a later need, or an existing state is deliberately left alone.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 窓は開けておいてください。
choices: You must not open the window.
questions.explanation: “窓は開けておいてください。” means “Please leave the window open.” in this example. The action is performed for a later need, or an existing state is deliberately left alone.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Completion and regret: てしまう
grammar.explanation:
てしまう can emphasize finishing an action or an unintended, regrettable outcome. The context determines which meaning is intended.

Formation: Verb て-form + しまう. Casual てしまう → ちゃう; でしまう → じゃう.

Usage and cautions: This can express complete finishing, regret, or an unintended event. Do not assume regret in every context: 全部食べてしまう can simply mean finishing it all. Tense and politeness belong to しまう: しまった, しまいました.

examples.ja: 財布を忘れてしまいました。
examples.en: Unfortunately, I forgot my wallet.

examples.ja: 宿題を全部やってしまいました。
examples.reading: しゅくだいをぜんぶやってしまいました。
examples.en: I finished all my homework.

examples.ja: 電車に傘を忘れてしまいました。
examples.reading: でんしゃにかさをわすれてしまいました。
examples.en: Unfortunately, I left my umbrella on the train.

questions.prompt: Choose the nuance of 割ってしまった in a regretful context.
choices: I am permitted to break it
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “I broke it, unfortunately”. てしまう can mark an unwelcome completed event.

questions.prompt: Choose an accidental deletion: 大切な写真を消し＿。
questions.explanation: 消してしまった presents a completed, regrettable deletion in this context, not preparation or prohibition.

questions.prompt: Which is the casual equivalent of 飲んでしまった?
questions.explanation: でしまった contracts to じゃった; どいた would represent でおいた, a different auxiliary.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 宿題を全部やってしまいました。
choices: I want someone to do all my homework.
I have not started my homework.
I am allowed to skip my homework.
questions.explanation: “宿題を全部やってしまいました。” means “I finished all my homework.” in this example. This can express complete finishing, regret, or an unintended event.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 電車に傘を忘れてしまいました。
choices: Unfortunately, I left my umbrella on the train.
I deliberately left an umbrella ready on the train.
I have never forgotten an umbrella.
I will buy an umbrella at the station.
questions.explanation: “電車に傘を忘れてしまいました。” means “Unfortunately, I left my umbrella on the train.” in this example. This can express complete finishing, regret, or an unintended event.

grammar.title: Potential forms
grammar.explanation:
Potential verbs express ability or possibility. Godan 書く becomes 書ける, ichidan 食べる becomes 食べられる, and する becomes できる.

Formation: Godan u-row → e-row + る: 読む→読める. Ichidan: 食べる→食べられる. する→できる; 来る→来られる.

Usage and cautions: Potential verbs inflect like ichidan verbs: 読めない, 読めました. The object can take が or を depending on context. Standard writing retains ら in 食べられる; casual ら抜き forms are widespread but not the formal target here. Potential is ability or possibility, not permission.

examples.ja: 私は漢字が読めます。
examples.en: I can read kanji.

examples.ja: ここから海が見えます。
examples.reading: ここからうみがみえます。
examples.en: The sea is visible from here.

examples.ja: 昨日は忙しくて、参加できませんでした。
examples.reading: きのうはいそがしくて、さんかできませんでした。
examples.en: I was busy yesterday and could not participate.

questions.prompt: Choose the standard potential of 食べる.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “食べられる”. 食べられる expresses ability; 食べさせる is causative and 食べよう volitional.

questions.prompt: Choose the potential form of 話す.
questions.explanation: 話す is godan: す changes to せ before る, producing 話せる; the other forms are passive, causative and volitional.

questions.prompt: Choose the standard potential of 来る, meaning “can come”.
questions.explanation: 来る has the irregular standard potential 来られる, read こられる.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: ここから海が見えます。
choices: The sea is visible from here.
I want to swim in the sea.
The sea cannot be seen from here.
I saw the sea only yesterday.
questions.explanation: “ここから海が見えます。” means “The sea is visible from here.” in this example. Potential verbs inflect like ichidan verbs: 読めない, 読めました.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 昨日は忙しくて、参加できませんでした。
choices: I can participate tomorrow because I am free.
I refused to let anyone participate yesterday.
I was busy yesterday and could not participate.
questions.explanation: “昨日は忙しくて、参加できませんでした。” means “I was busy yesterday and could not participate.” in this example. Potential verbs inflect like ichidan verbs: 読めない, 読めました.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Intention: つもり
grammar.explanation:
Use dictionary form plus つもり for an intention and ない-form plus つもり for an intention not to act. This is stronger than a passing wish.

Formation: Dictionary verb + つもりだ; negative verb + つもりだ expresses an intention not to act.

Usage and cautions: This expresses a settled personal intention, not a publicly fixed timetable. Do not use the plain past form for a future plan. つもりだった can describe a past intention that was not realized. 行くつもりはない denies having the intention and can sound stronger than 行かないつもり.

examples.ja: 来年、日本で働くつもりです。
examples.en: I intend to work in Japan next year.

examples.ja: 夏休みに北海道を旅行するつもりです。
examples.reading: なつやすみにほっかいどうをりょこうするつもりです。
examples.en: I intend to travel around Hokkaido during summer vacation.

examples.ja: 今日はお酒を飲まないつもりです。
examples.reading: きょうはおさけをのまないつもりです。
examples.en: I intend not to drink alcohol today.

questions.prompt: Choose an intention not to go.
choices: 行かなければなりません
行ったことがあります
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “行かないつもりです”. ないつもり states the speaker's intended non-action.

questions.prompt: Complete an intention to study: 毎日、日本語を勉強＿つもりです。
questions.explanation: Future intention uses dictionary form 勉強する before つもり, not the past or polite form.

questions.prompt: Choose a past intention that context may show was not fulfilled.
choices: 早く帰るつもりでした。
早く帰ったことがあります。
早く帰ってもいいです。
questions.explanation: つもりでした reports what the intention was; it does not itself guarantee that the early return happened.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 夏休みに北海道を旅行するつもりです。
choices: I have already traveled around Hokkaido.
I am required to travel around Hokkaido.
Hokkaido is planning a summer holiday.
I intend to travel around Hokkaido during summer vacation.
questions.explanation: “夏休みに北海道を旅行するつもりです。” means “I intend to travel around Hokkaido during summer vacation.” in this example. This expresses a settled personal intention, not a publicly fixed timetable.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 今日はお酒を飲まないつもりです。
choices: I intended to drink alcohol yesterday.
I intend not to drink alcohol today.
I cannot drink any alcohol today.
questions.explanation: “今日はお酒を飲まないつもりです。” means “I intend not to drink alcohol today.” in this example. This expresses a settled personal intention, not a publicly fixed timetable.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Plans: 予定
grammar.explanation:
Dictionary form or noun + の followed by 予定 describes a scheduled plan. It often sounds more externally arranged than つもり.

Formation: Dictionary verb + 予定だ; noun + の + 予定だ. Negative plans can use ない予定だ.

Usage and cautions: 予定 presents a schedule or arrangement, often involving other people or an event. Contrast personal resolve with つもり. The event verb remains plain even when 予定です is polite. A schedule is not a guarantee: circumstances can change it.

examples.ja: 会議は三時に始まる予定です。
examples.en: The meeting is scheduled to start at three.

examples.ja: 飛行機は十時に到着する予定です。
examples.reading: ひこうきはじゅうじにとうちゃくするよていです。
examples.en: The plane is scheduled to arrive at ten.

examples.ja: 試験は来月の予定です。
examples.reading: しけんはらいげつのよていです。
examples.en: The exam is scheduled for next month.

questions.prompt: Complete: 来週、出発する＿です。
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “予定”. 予定 names a scheduled plan after dictionary-form 出発する.

questions.prompt: Use the noun connection: 出発は明日＿予定です。
questions.explanation: A noun such as 明日 connects to 予定 with の; a dictionary verb would connect directly.

questions.prompt: Choose a formally scheduled meeting start.
choices: 会議は九時に始まったことがあります。
会議は九時に始まってみます。
会議は九時に始まりたがっています。
会議は九時に始まる予定です。
questions.explanation: 始まる予定です states the arranged start; experience, trial and third-person desire do not express a timetable.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 飛行機は十時に到着する予定です。
choices: The plane is forbidden to arrive at ten.
I hope to become a pilot at ten.
The plane is scheduled to arrive at ten.
The plane arrived at ten yesterday.
questions.explanation: “飛行機は十時に到着する予定です。” means “The plane is scheduled to arrive at ten.” in this example. 予定 presents a schedule or arrangement, often involving other people or an event.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 試験は来月の予定です。
choices: There will be an exam every day this month.
The exam is scheduled for next month.
I plan to cancel every exam.
questions.explanation: “試験は来月の予定です。” means “The exam is scheduled for next month.” in this example. 予定 presents a schedule or arrangement, often involving other people or an event.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Advice: ほうがいい
grammar.explanation:
Verb past + ほうがいい gives advice to act; ない-form + ほうがいい advises against acting. It may sound strong without softening.

Formation: Plain past verb + ほうがいい for positive advice; negative verb + ほうがいい for advice against an action.

Usage and cautions: The past form in positive advice does not necessarily mean the advised action already happened. This can sound forceful, especially unsolicited. と思います can soften it. Do not use なくてもいい when you mean “should not”: that only removes obligation.

examples.ja: 早く寝たほうがいいです。
examples.en: You should go to bed early.

examples.ja: 熱があるなら、病院に行ったほうがいいです。
examples.reading: ねつがあるなら、びょういんにいったほうがいいです。
examples.en: If you have a fever, you should go to a hospital.

examples.ja: 夜遅くにコーヒーを飲まないほうがいいです。
examples.reading: よるおそくにコーヒーをのまないほうがいいです。
examples.en: You should avoid drinking coffee late at night.

questions.prompt: Choose advice not to smoke.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “吸わないほうがいい”. The negative form before ほうがいい advises avoiding the action.

questions.prompt: Give positive advice: もっと休ん＿ほうがいいです。
questions.explanation: 休む has the past form 休んだ; past + ほうがいい gives advice to rest more.

questions.prompt: Advise against carrying heavy luggage: 重い荷物を＿ほうがいい。
questions.explanation: 持たないほうがいい recommends not carrying it; 持ったほうがいい would recommend carrying it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 熱があるなら、病院に行ったほうがいいです。
choices: You need not visit a hospital even with a fever.
If you have a fever, you should go to a hospital.
If you have a fever, you must not go to a hospital.
You have already gone to a hospital for a fever.
questions.explanation: “熱があるなら、病院に行ったほうがいいです。” means “If you have a fever, you should go to a hospital.” in this example. The past form in positive advice does not necessarily mean the advised action already happened.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 夜遅くにコーヒーを飲まないほうがいいです。
choices: You should avoid drinking coffee late at night.
You do not have to drink coffee every morning.
You should drink coffee late at night.
I used to drink coffee late at night.
questions.explanation: “夜遅くにコーヒーを飲まないほうがいいです。” means “You should avoid drinking coffee late at night.” in this example. The past form in positive advice does not necessarily mean the advised action already happened.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Obligation: なければならない
grammar.explanation:
Replace the final ない of a negative verb with なければならない to express necessity. Casual speech often shortens this construction.

Formation: Verb ない-form minus ない + なければならない. Polite ending: なければなりません.

Usage and cautions: The double negative expresses obligation: “if not doing it, that will not do”. Casual speech may shorten it to なきゃ or なくちゃ when the obligation is understood. Do not confuse this with なくてもいい, which removes obligation, or てはいけない, which prohibits action.

examples.ja: 薬を飲まなければなりません。
examples.en: I must take my medicine.

examples.ja: 明日までに宿題を出さなければなりません。
examples.reading: あしたまでにしゅくだいをださなければなりません。
examples.en: I must submit my homework by tomorrow.

examples.ja: 毎日、この薬を飲まなければなりません。
examples.reading: まいにち、このくすりをのまなければなりません。
examples.en: I must take this medicine every day.

questions.prompt: Choose 'must study'.
choices: 勉強しなければならない
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “勉強しなければならない”. なければならない means necessary; the others mean optional and forbidden.

questions.prompt: Choose the obligation form of 来る.
questions.explanation: 来なければならない means one must come; the alternatives express no obligation, prohibition and experience.

questions.prompt: Complete “I must go”: 行か＿なりません。
questions.explanation: 行かない becomes 行かなければ; followed by なりません it expresses an obligation to go.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 明日までに宿題を出さなければなりません。
choices: I must submit my homework by tomorrow.
I may submit my homework whenever I want.
I must not submit my homework tomorrow.
questions.explanation: “明日までに宿題を出さなければなりません。” means “I must submit my homework by tomorrow.” in this example. The double negative expresses obligation: “if not doing it, that will not do”.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 毎日、この薬を飲まなければなりません。
choices: I am not allowed to take this medicine.
I do not need to take this medicine daily.
I must take this medicine every day.
questions.explanation: “毎日、この薬を飲まなければなりません。” means “I must take this medicine every day.” in this example. The double negative expresses obligation: “if not doing it, that will not do”.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: No obligation: なくてもいい
grammar.explanation:
Verb negative ない becomes なくてもいい to say there is no need to do something. This is permission not to act, not a prohibition.

Formation: Verb ない-form: replace ない with なくてもいい. Polite: なくてもいいです.

Usage and cautions: This permits not doing something while leaving the option to do it. It is not a ban. Compare 行ってはいけない “must not go” and 行かなければならない “must go”. In a question, なくてもいいですか asks whether skipping the action is acceptable.

examples.ja: 明日は来なくてもいいです。
examples.en: You do not have to come tomorrow.

examples.ja: 全部覚えなくてもいいです。
examples.reading: ぜんぶおぼえなくてもいいです。
examples.en: You do not have to memorize everything.

examples.ja: 明日は早く起きなくてもいいです。
examples.reading: あしたははやくおきなくてもいいです。
examples.en: You do not need to get up early tomorrow.

questions.prompt: What does 払わなくてもいい mean?
choices: You do not have to pay
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “You do not have to pay”. なくてもいい removes obligation; it does not forbid paying.

questions.prompt: Ask if writing a name is optional: 名前を書か＿いいですか。
questions.explanation: 書かなくてもいいですか asks whether not writing is acceptable; it does not ask permission to write.

questions.prompt: Which means that attendance is optional, not forbidden?
choices: 参加しなくてもいいです。
参加してはいけません。
参加しなければなりません。
questions.explanation: しなくてもいい removes the obligation to participate; prohibition and inability are different meanings.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 全部覚えなくてもいいです。
choices: You do not have to memorize everything.
questions.explanation: “全部覚えなくてもいいです。” means “You do not have to memorize everything.” in this example. This permits not doing something while leaving the option to do it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 明日は早く起きなくてもいいです。
choices: You cannot get up early tomorrow.
You do not need to get up early tomorrow.
You must get up early tomorrow.
questions.explanation: “明日は早く起きなくてもいいです。” means “You do not need to get up early tomorrow.” in this example. This permits not doing something while leaving the option to do it.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Conditional: たら
grammar.explanation:
Attach ら to the plain past form to introduce a condition or a time when something has happened. The main clause can contain a request or intention.

Formation: Plain past form + ら: 行ったら, 飲んだら, 安かったら, 静かだったら.

Usage and cautions: たら can introduce an imagined condition or a time after a future event. Requests and intentions are possible in the main clause. In the temporal reading, the first event is completed before the second. Do not use a ます-form directly before たら.

examples.ja: 駅に着いたら、電話してください。
examples.en: When you arrive at the station, please call.

examples.ja: 仕事が終わったら、買い物に行きます。
examples.reading: しごとがおわったら、かいものにいきます。
examples.en: When work finishes, I will go shopping.

examples.ja: 安かったら、このかばんを買います。
examples.reading: やすかったら、このかばんをかいます。
examples.en: If it is cheap, I will buy this bag.

questions.prompt: Complete: 雨が降っ＿、家にいます。
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “たら”. 降ったら makes the rain a condition for staying home.

questions.prompt: Complete a temporal condition: 家に帰っ＿、手を洗ってください。
questions.explanation: 帰ったら means once you have returned home; the request follows that completed arrival.

questions.prompt: Choose the conditional form of 暇だ.
questions.explanation: A な-adjective or noun predicate forms the past with だった, then adds ら: 暇だったら.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 仕事が終わったら、買い物に行きます。
choices: I finished work because I went shopping.
I will shop even if work never finishes.
When work finishes, I will go shopping.
questions.explanation: “仕事が終わったら、買い物に行きます。” means “When work finishes, I will go shopping.” in this example. たら can introduce an imagined condition or a time after a future event.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 安かったら、このかばんを買います。
choices: This bag became cheap after I bought it.
If it is cheap, I will buy this bag.
Although it is cheap, I will not buy this bag.
I bought this bag because it was expensive.
questions.explanation: “安かったら、このかばんを買います。” means “If it is cheap, I will buy this bag.” in this example. たら can introduce an imagined condition or a time after a future event.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Concession: ても
grammar.explanation:
The て-form plus も means even if or even though. It indicates that the following result holds despite the preceding condition.

Formation: Verb て-form + も; い-adjective くても; noun / な-adjective でも.

Usage and cautions: The main result remains true despite the condition. This differs from たら, which makes the result depend on that condition. The statement may be hypothetical “even if” or factual “although”; context decides. Negative verbs form なくても.

examples.ja: 雨が降っても、行きます。
examples.en: Even if it rains, I will go.

examples.ja: 忙しくても、朝ご飯を食べます。
examples.reading: いそがしくても、あさごはんをたべます。
examples.en: Even when busy, I eat breakfast.

examples.ja: 雨でも、試合はあります。
examples.reading: あめでも、しあいはあります。
examples.en: The match will take place even if it rains.

questions.prompt: Choose a concession: 高く＿買います。
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “ても”. い-adjective 高い becomes 高くても: even if expensive.

questions.prompt: Complete a noun concession: 休み＿、早く起きます。
questions.explanation: A noun takes でも: 休みでも means even on a day off; ても attaches to a verb て-form instead.

questions.prompt: Choose “even if I do not understand”.
questions.explanation: The negative concession changes ない to なくても; なければ instead introduces a condition.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 忙しくても、朝ご飯を食べます。
choices: I became busy after eating breakfast.
Even when busy, I eat breakfast.
I eat breakfast only when I have free time.
Because I am busy, I skip breakfast.
questions.explanation: “忙しくても、朝ご飯を食べます。” means “Even when busy, I eat breakfast.” in this example. The main result remains true despite the condition.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 雨でも、試合はあります。
choices: The match will take place even if it rains.
The match will take place only if it rains.
The match was canceled because of rain.
There will be no rain during the match.
questions.explanation: “雨でも、試合はあります。” means “The match will take place even if it rains.” in this example. The main result remains true despite the condition.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Natural consequences: と
grammar.explanation:
Plain nonpast + と introduces a predictable consequence, rule, or automatic result. Requests and personal intentions normally require a different conditional.

Formation: Plain nonpast + と + predictable result. Negative conditions can use ないと.

Usage and cautions: This suits rules, machine operations and repeated natural consequences. A main-clause invitation, command or intention normally calls for たら or another conditional. A past narrative can also use と for a discovery, but that is distinct from the basic automatic-result use.

examples.ja: このボタンを押すと、ドアが開きます。
examples.en: If you press this button, the door opens.

examples.ja: この道をまっすぐ行くと、駅があります。
examples.reading: このみちをまっすぐいくと、えきがあります。
examples.en: If you go straight along this road, you will find the station.

examples.ja: 氷を温めると、水になります。
examples.reading: こおりをあたためると、みずになります。
examples.en: When ice is heated, it becomes water.

questions.prompt: Choose a natural consequence connector: 春になる＿、暖かくなる。
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “と”. と suits a predictable seasonal consequence.

questions.prompt: Choose the connector for a machine’s automatic result: お金を入れる＿、切符が出ます。
questions.explanation: と naturally links inserting money with the machine producing a ticket as a regular result.

questions.prompt: Which main clause is unsuitable for the basic automatic-result と pattern?
questions.explanation: 電話してください is a request, not an automatic consequence; use a conditional such as 着いたら for a request after arrival.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: この道をまっすぐ行くと、駅があります。
choices: If you go straight along this road, you will find the station.
You must go straight because the station is closed.
The station moves whenever I walk.
Please build a station on this road.
questions.explanation: “この道をまっすぐ行くと、駅があります。” means “If you go straight along this road, you will find the station.” in this example. This suits rules, machine operations and repeated natural consequences.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 氷を温めると、水になります。
choices: Even when heated, ice never melts.
Heat the water if you want ice.
Water becomes ice because it is heated.
When ice is heated, it becomes water.
questions.explanation: “氷を温めると、水になります。” means “When ice is heated, it becomes water.” in this example. This suits rules, machine operations and repeated natural consequences.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Simultaneous actions: ながら
grammar.explanation:
Attach ながら to a verb's ます-stem for two simultaneous actions by the same subject. The action after ながら is normally the main one.

Formation: Verb ます-stem + ながら + main action. Tense is normally carried by the final predicate.

Usage and cautions: The same person performs both actions in the simultaneous-action pattern. The action after ながら is the main one. Do not use this to join unrelated events performed by different people. Distinguish the advanced concessive meaning “although” in expressions such as 残念ながら.

examples.ja: 音楽を聞きながら勉強します。
examples.en: I study while listening to music.

examples.ja: テレビを見ながら夕飯を食べました。
examples.reading: テレビをみながらゆうはんをたべました。
examples.en: I ate dinner while watching television.

examples.ja: 歌を歌いながら歩きます。
examples.reading: うたをうたいながらあるきます。
examples.en: I walk while singing a song.

questions.prompt: Complete: 歩き＿話します。
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “ながら”. 歩き is the stem; ながら introduces the accompanying activity.

questions.prompt: Complete simultaneous actions: コーヒーを飲み＿、新聞を読みます。
questions.explanation: 飲み is the ます-stem and ながら makes drinking the accompanying action while reading.

questions.prompt: In 音楽を聞きながら料理する, what is the main action?
questions.explanation: The main action comes after ながら, so 料理する is central and listening accompanies it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: テレビを見ながら夕飯を食べました。
choices: I ate dinner after turning off the television.
Someone else watched television while I cooked.
I will eat dinner before watching television.
I ate dinner while watching television.
questions.explanation: “テレビを見ながら夕飯を食べました。” means “I ate dinner while watching television.” in this example. The same person performs both actions in the simultaneous-action pattern.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 歌を歌いながら歩きます。
choices: Another person sings while I sleep.
I walk while singing a song.
I sing only after I stop walking.
questions.explanation: “歌を歌いながら歩きます。” means “I walk while singing a song.” in this example. The same person performs both actions in the simultaneous-action pattern.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Purpose: ために
grammar.explanation:
Dictionary form + ために states a deliberate goal. Use noun + のために for a beneficiary or purpose. Potential verbs often favor ように instead.

Formation: Dictionary verb + ために + preparatory action; noun + のために for a purpose or beneficiary.

Usage and cautions: The goal normally involves a controllable action, with the same actor for the goal and its preparation. For an ability or nonvolitional outcome, ように is often better: 読めるように練習する. ため can also mark cause elsewhere; identify the relation from context.

examples.ja: 留学するために、お金を貯めています。
examples.en: I am saving money to study abroad.

examples.ja: 家族のために、毎日働いています。
examples.reading: かぞくのために、まいにちはたらいています。
examples.en: I work every day for my family.

examples.ja: 試験に合格するために、復習します。
examples.reading: しけんにごうかくするために、ふくしゅうします。
examples.en: I review in order to pass the exam.

questions.prompt: Choose a purpose: 車を買う＿、貯金する。
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “ために”. ために links saving money to the intended goal of buying a car.

questions.prompt: Complete a noun purpose: 健康＿ために、毎朝歩きます。
questions.explanation: A noun connects with の: 健康のために means for the sake of health.

questions.prompt: Choose the purpose of saving in 留学するために貯金しています.
questions.explanation: The clause before ために states the goal, 留学する; 貯金する is the means toward it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 家族のために、毎日働いています。
choices: I work only when my family works.
My family worked for me yesterday.
I work every day for my family.
My family prevents me from working every day.
questions.explanation: “家族のために、毎日働いています。” means “I work every day for my family.” in this example. The goal normally involves a controllable action, with the same actor for the goal and its preparation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 試験に合格するために、復習します。
choices: I am forbidden to review for the exam.
I review in order to pass the exam.
I passed the exam because I stopped reviewing.
I review despite already failing the exam.
questions.explanation: “試験に合格するために、復習します。” means “I review in order to pass the exam.” in this example. The goal normally involves a controllable action, with the same actor for the goal and its preparation.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Reported information: そうだ
grammar.explanation:
Plain form + そうだ reports information heard or read. Do not confuse it with stem + そうだ, which describes an appearance.

Formation: Plain clause + そうだ: 降るそうだ, 降ったそうだ, おいしいそうだ. Noun / な-adjective: だそうだ.

Usage and cautions: Hearsay preserves the whole plain predicate, including adjective い or copula だ. Cite a source with によると when useful. Appearance uses a stem instead: おいしそうだ. Do not infer the speaker has personally verified what is reported.

examples.ja: 天気予報によると、明日は雨が降るそうです。
examples.en: According to the forecast, it will rain tomorrow.

examples.ja: 友達によると、その店は安いそうです。
examples.reading: ともだちによると、そのみせはやすいそうです。
examples.en: According to a friend, that shop is inexpensive.

examples.ja: 田中さんは来週休むそうです。
examples.reading: たなかさんはらいしゅうやすむそうです。
examples.en: I hear Tanaka will take time off next week.

questions.prompt: Which reports what someone said?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “おいしいそうだ”. おいしいそうだ retains final い for hearsay; おいしそうだ means it looks tasty.

questions.prompt: Report “the town is quiet”: 町は静か＿そうです。
questions.explanation: Hearsay retains the plain copula: 静かだそうです; appearance would be 静かそうです.

questions.prompt: Choose hearsay about a completed departure.
choices: もう出発したそうです。
questions.explanation: 出発したそうです reports that departure already happened; 出発しそうです describes an imminent appearance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 友達によると、その店は安いそうです。
choices: The shop used to be expensive.
According to a friend, that shop is inexpensive.
The shop looks inexpensive to me.
My friend wants to lower the shop’s prices.
questions.explanation: “友達によると、その店は安いそうです。” means “According to a friend, that shop is inexpensive.” in this example. Hearsay preserves the whole plain predicate, including adjective い or copula だ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 田中さんは来週休むそうです。
choices: I hear Tanaka will take time off next week.
Tanaka looks as if they are resting now.
Please let Tanaka rest next week.
Tanaka took time off last week.
questions.explanation: “田中さんは来週休むそうです。” means “I hear Tanaka will take time off next week.” in this example. Hearsay preserves the whole plain predicate, including adjective い or copula だ.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Appearance: そうだ
grammar.explanation:
Attach そうだ to a verb stem or adjective stem to describe an apparent tendency or appearance. いい becomes よさそう; ない becomes なさそう.

Formation: Verb ます-stem + そうだ; い-adjective minus い + そうだ; な-adjective + そうだ.

Usage and cautions: This judges visible signs or an apparent likelihood, rather than relaying someone’s words. Exceptions include よさそう and なさそう. Modify a noun with そうな and an action with そうに. Do not remove the final い of an adjective when forming hearsay instead.

examples.ja: このケーキはおいしそうです。
examples.en: This cake looks delicious.

examples.ja: 空が暗くて、雨が降りそうです。
examples.reading: そらがくらくて、あめがふりそうです。
examples.en: The sky is dark, and it looks likely to rain.

examples.ja: その仕事は大変そうですね。
examples.reading: そのしごとはたいへんそうですね。
examples.en: That job looks demanding.

questions.prompt: Choose 'looks cold' from 寒い.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “寒そう”. Appearance removes the adjective's final い; 寒いそう is hearsay.

questions.prompt: Choose “looks good” from いい.
questions.explanation: Appearance そう uses the exceptional form よさそう; いいそう is a hearsay form in the right context.

questions.prompt: Modify a noun: おいしそう＿パンですね。
questions.explanation: Appearance そう behaves like a な-adjective before nouns: おいしそうなパン.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 空が暗くて、雨が降りそうです。
choices: The sky is dark, and it looks likely to rain.
I heard that it rained yesterday.
I want it to rain tomorrow.
questions.explanation: “空が暗くて、雨が降りそうです。” means “The sky is dark, and it looks likely to rain.” in this example. This judges visible signs or an apparent likelihood, rather than relaying someone’s words.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: その仕事は大変そうですね。
choices: I heard that job was easy.
Please make that job more demanding.
questions.explanation: “その仕事は大変そうですね。” means “That job looks demanding.” in this example. This judges visible signs or an apparent likelihood, rather than relaying someone’s words.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Giving and receiving
grammar.explanation:
あげる describes giving away from one's side, くれる giving toward one's side, and もらう receiving. With て-forms they also express benefits.

Formation: Giver が recipient に thing を あげる / くれる. Recipient が giver に / から thing を もらう.

Usage and cautions: くれる directs a benefit toward the speaker or the speaker’s group; あげる views it outward. もらう makes the recipient the subject. Verb て-forms extend these to helpful actions. Do not use あげる about helping a superior without considering its potentially patronizing tone.

examples.ja: 友達が宿題を手伝ってくれました。
examples.en: My friend kindly helped me with my homework.

examples.ja: 私は弟に本をあげました。
examples.reading: わたしはおとうとにほんをあげました。
examples.en: I gave my younger brother a book.

examples.ja: 私は友達に駅まで送ってもらいました。
examples.reading: わたしはともだちにえきまでおくってもらいました。
examples.en: A friend kindly took me to the station.

questions.prompt: Choose a friend giving me a book: 友達が私に本を＿。
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “くれた”. くれる views giving from the recipient's side, here the speaker.

questions.prompt: The recipient is the subject: 私は姉からプレゼントを＿。
questions.explanation: 私は is the receiver and 姉から marks the giver, so use もらいました.

questions.prompt: Choose a benefit toward the speaker: 先生が説明して＿。
questions.explanation: 先生が is the helpful actor, so くれました fits; いただく would make the speaker the receiving subject.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 私は弟に本をあげました。
choices: My younger brother gave me a book.
I borrowed a book from my younger brother.
My younger brother sold my book.
I gave my younger brother a book.
questions.explanation: “私は弟に本をあげました。” means “I gave my younger brother a book.” in this example. くれる directs a benefit toward the speaker or the speaker’s group; あげる views it outward.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 私は友達に駅まで送ってもらいました。
choices: My friend refused to go to the station.
I sent a parcel to my friend’s station.
A friend kindly took me to the station.
I took a friend to the station.
questions.explanation: “私は友達に駅まで送ってもらいました。” means “A friend kindly took me to the station.” in this example. くれる directs a benefit toward the speaker or the speaker’s group; あげる views it outward.

grammar.title: Nominalizing with の・こと
grammar.explanation:
の and こと turn a clause into a noun-like expression. Preferences often use のが; fixed expressions such as ことができる require こと.

Formation: Plain clause + の / こと turns an action into a noun phrase. Fixed ability pattern: dictionary verb + ことができる.

Usage and cautions: の often presents a directly experienced event or a preferred activity; こと often presents an abstract activity or rule. They are not interchangeable in every fixed expression. Keep the embedded predicate plain, and retain its internal particles: 本を読むのが好き.

examples.ja: 料理をするのが好きです。
examples.en: I like cooking.

examples.ja: 早く起きるのは大変です。
examples.reading: はやくおきるのはたいへんです。
examples.en: Getting up early is hard.

examples.ja: ここで切符を買うことができます。
examples.reading: ここできっぷをかうことができます。
examples.en: You can buy tickets here.

questions.prompt: Complete a standard ability expression: 泳ぐ＿ができる。
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “こと”. ことができる is the established pattern meaning 'can do'.

questions.prompt: Nominalize an enjoyed activity: 本を読む＿が好きです。
questions.explanation: 読むの turns reading into the noun-like activity that is liked; the other choices do not form this intended preference expression.

questions.prompt: Complete a fixed rule expression: ここでは靴を脱ぐ＿になっています。
questions.explanation: ことになっている presents an established rule or arrangement; this fixed expression uses こと.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 早く起きるのは大変です。
choices: I got up early with no difficulty.
Someone made me get up early yesterday.
It is forbidden to get up early.
questions.explanation: “早く起きるのは大変です。” means “Getting up early is hard.” in this example. の often presents a directly experienced event or a preferred activity; こと often presents an abstract activity or rule.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: ここで切符を買うことができます。
questions.explanation: “ここで切符を買うことができます。” means “You can buy tickets here.” in this example. の often presents a directly experienced event or a preferred activity; こと often presents an abstract activity or rule.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.
